meta.trial_name: OMEMI (OMega-3 fatty acids in Elderly with Myocardial Infarction)
meta.drug: marine n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (Pikasol, Orkla Health), 1.8 g/day = 930 mg EPA + 660 mg DHA in 3 capsules once daily, versus corn-oil placebo, added to standard post-MI care
meta.sponsor: Oslo University Hospital (investigator-initiated; grants from Stein Erik Hagen Foundation, Olav Thons Foundation and Tom Wilhelmsen Foundation; capsules and placebo supplied by Orkla Health)
meta.mechanism: Mixed EPA/DHA fish-oil supplement intended to raise serum omega-3 levels (serum phospholipid EPA +87%, DHA +16% median) and to lower cardiovascular risk through hypothesised triglyceride-lowering, antiarrhythmic, antithrombotic and anti-inflammatory effects. No single molecular target. At 1.8 g/day in patients with normal triglycerides (mean 1.26 mmol/L) the lipid effect was small: median between-group triglyceride difference 13.2%, no LDL-C change (S4). target_symbol LPL is used, as in the STRENGTH, REDUCE-IT and ASCEND cases, only as the human-genetic proxy for the triglyceride-lowering pathway (Ference 2019, S11), not as a confirmed drug target.
meta.modality: dietary supplement / small molecule (oral fish-oil capsules, 1.8 g EPA+DHA once daily)
meta.indication: secondary prevention after a recent (2-8 weeks) acute myocardial infarction in elderly patients aged 70-82 years (Norway)

n_randomized.quote: In total, 1027 patients were randomized. Follow-up data were available for 1014 patients who were included in the intention-to-treat analysis.
n_randomized.note: ITT analysis: 505 n-3 PUFA vs 509 placebo (S4 Results). ACC summary (S6) gives 513 vs 514 randomized. Registry S3 enrollment 1027 (ACTUAL). Planned 1100 after amendment (S4) and 1400 in the design paper (S5): recruitment fell short.

median_followup.quote: The primary endpoint was a composite of nonfatal AMI, unscheduled revascularization, stroke, all-cause death, heart failure hospitalization after 2 years.
median_followup.note: Fixed 2-year follow-up; S4: 'Patients without events were censored after two years of follow-up or at the date of last participation to a visit for patients lost to follow-up.' Median not reported. DERIVED mean event-free follow-up about 1.7 years (108 events / 12.4 per 100 patient-years = about 871 patient-years in 505 patients, S4).

primary_endpoint.value: Composite of non-fatal MI, unscheduled revascularization, stroke, all-cause death or hospitalization for heart failure within 2 years (secondary: new-onset atrial fibrillation; safety: major bleeding BARC>=2)
primary_endpoint.quote: The pre-specified primary efficacy outcome was the first major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE), consisted of a composite of non-fatal MI, unscheduled revascularization, stroke or all-cause death. While recruitment was still ongoing, hospitalization for heart failure (HF) was added to the definition of MACE by protocol amendment.
primary_endpoint.note: Endpoint changed during recruitment, 'potentially to increase statistical power of the trial' (S4). Registry S3 primary outcome: 'Combined total mortality, first event of non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, revascularization or hospital admission for new or worsened heart failure.' Design paper S5 had no HF component. All-cause death and HF hospitalization are components a lipid mechanism acts on weakly.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age 70-82 years; hospitalised for acute MI of any type, randomised 2-8 weeks after the index MI; exclusion: n-3 intolerance, other trial, disease incompatible with adherence, life expectancy <2 years. No triglyceride entry criterion; low-dose cod liver oil (one child spoon/day) permitted.
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Hospitalized patients between 70 and 82 years old who were able to provide verbal and written informed consent, were screened during admission for the index AMI of any type at four centers in Norway
inclusion_key_criteria.note: S4: baseline visit 'was later changed up to 2-8 weeks to enhance inclusion rate'. 'one child spoon of cod liver oil was permitted'. 415 (41.3%) reported some n-3 PUFA supplement use at enrolment. Registry S3: minimum age 70, maximum 82.

planned_events.note: NOT FOUND: no planned event count is stated. Sizing was by patient number (500 per arm, 1100 total, S4). DERIVED only: 35% placebo and 26.25% active 2-year rates in 1000 patients would give about 306 events; observed 210 (108 + 102).

assumed_rrr.quote: With the protocol amendment including hospitalization for HF in the primary outcome, we anticipated an increase in the two-year event rate from 20% to 35%, but reduced the estimated effect of the intervention from 30% to 25%.
assumed_rrr.note: Original design (S4 and pre-readout S5): 30% reduction in MACE from 20% to 14% over two years, 611 patients per arm, 1400 in total (S5). Observed placebo 2-year rate about 20.0%, far below the 35% assumed after the amendment.

power.quote: With an α of 0.05 and a power of 80 %, 611 patients would be required in each study arm with an estimated dropout rate of 10%.
power.note: 80% stated for the original calculation; the amendment kept the framework (500 per arm, 1100 total). DERIVED (not from a source): with 210 events, power to detect HR 0.75 at two-sided 0.05 is about 55%. Authors (S4): 'we cannot rule out Type 2 errors as the trial ended up not being sufficiently powered to answer the original research question.'

alpha.quote: A two-tailed P value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

stopped_early.note: Ran to scheduled completion: registry overallStatus COMPLETED, primary completion 2020-06-26 (S3). Last patient randomised July 5, 2018 (S4). No interim analyses planned (S5: 'No interim analyses are planned').

baseline.note: Published abstract S1: 'mean triglycerides were 111.4±61.9 mg/dL'. Table 1: 1.3 ± 0.8 (n-3) vs 1.2 ± 0.6 (placebo) mmol/L. Patients were NOT selected for high triglycerides.
LDL-C. 1.95 = average of the two group means (DERIVED). Statin use 96.6% vs 96.3%.

baseline.unit: % weight of serum phospholipid fatty acids (EPA; 2.8 n-3, 2.9 placebo)
baseline.note: Exposure marker. Discussion: baseline median levels (2.5% EPA, 5.6% DHA) 'are notably higher than corresponding values from population studies in the USA (0.5 % EPA and 2.9 % DHA)', suggesting high background n-3 intake in Norway.
NOT FOUND: baseline apoB, non-HDL-C and Lp(a) not reported.

biomarker_effects.method: routine hospital laboratory, fasting; relative change from baseline compared by Mann-Whitney U test
biomarker_effects.quote: Triglycerides changes by median (Q1, Q3) were -8.1% (-27.5%, +15.3%) in the n-3 PUFA group vs +5.1% (-17.0%, +33.3%) in the placebo group (p<0.001); between-group median absolute difference 13.2%.
biomarker_effects.note: change_pct = between-group difference in median percent change (13.2 percentage points). change_abs DERIVED: -13.2% x baseline mean 1.26 mmol/L = -0.166 mmol/L (= -14.7 mg/dL). Discussion: 'modest reduction in triglycerides in the n-3 PUFA group compared to the placebo group (median 13 %)', less than earlier n-3 studies in younger patients with higher baseline triglycerides. Read in the accepted manuscript; the version of record was not read.

biomarker_effects.method: routine hospital laboratory; median relative change from baseline
biomarker_effects.note: Not significant. change_pct DERIVED: 0% - 0.7% = -0.7 percentage points; change_abs DERIVED: -0.7% x 1.95 mmol/L = -0.014 mmol/L. Spacing as in source PDF text.

biomarker_effects.unit: % relative change from baseline (n-3 group; placebo -13%)
biomarker_effects.method: gas chromatography, Lipid Research Laboratory, Aalborg; n=881
biomarker_effects.quote: Median changes in eicosapentaenoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid were +87% and +16% for n-3 PUFA versus -13% and -8% for placebo.
biomarker_effects.note: Exposure/adherence marker, not sized. Within-group medians, not a placebo-adjusted difference. S4 Discussion compares the '113% between-group difference in increase' in OMEMI with 386% in REDUCE-IT.

biomarker_effects.unit: % relative change from baseline (n-3 group; placebo -8%)
biomarker_effects.quote: Median changes in eicosapentaenoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid were +87% and +16% for n-3 PUFA versus -13% and -8% for placebo.

biomarker_effects.note: NOT FOUND: no phase 2 programme (over-the-counter supplement). Pre-readout class evidence: pharmacological triglyceride lowering needs >3 g/day EPA+DHA (AHA advisory S10).

NOT FOUND: apoB, non-HDL-C and HDL-C changes not reported in the main paper. Secondary analysis S8: greater EPA/DHA increases 'were associated with decreasing triglycerides, increasing high-density lipoprotein cholesterol'.

hr.quote: The primary endpoint occurred in 108 (21.4%) patients on n-3 PUFA versus 102 (20.0%) on placebo (hazard ratio, 1.08 [95% CI, 0.82-1.41]; P=0.60).
hr.note: Version of record (published abstract, read via Europe PMC). The author accepted manuscript S4 and TCTMD S7 give HR 1.07 (0.82-1.40 in S4, 0.82-1.41 in S7), p=0.62. Per-protocol (n=893) similar. All-cause mortality 28 vs 28, HR 1.01 (0.60-1.71).

ci_low.quote: The primary endpoint occurred in 108 (21.4%) patients on n-3 PUFA versus 102 (20.0%) on placebo (hazard ratio, 1.08 [95% CI, 0.82-1.41]; P=0.60).

ci_high.quote: The primary endpoint occurred in 108 (21.4%) patients on n-3 PUFA versus 102 (20.0%) on placebo (hazard ratio, 1.08 [95% CI, 0.82-1.41]; P=0.60).

p.quote: The primary endpoint occurred in 108 (21.4%) patients on n-3 PUFA versus 102 (20.0%) on placebo (hazard ratio, 1.08 [95% CI, 0.82-1.41]; P=0.60).

events_treatment.quote: The primary endpoint occurred in 108 (21.4%) patients on n-3 PUFA

safety_signals.value: New-onset atrial fibrillation numerically higher: 28 (7.2%) vs 15 (4.0%), HR 1.84 (0.98-3.45), P=0.06
safety_signals.quote: The secondary endpoint occurred in 28 (7.2%) patients on n-3 PUFA versus 15 (4.0%) on placebo (1.84 [0.98-3.45]; P=0.06).
safety_signals.note: Among 759 patients free of AF at baseline. Kalstad at AHA (S7): 'We cannot rule out potential harm in increasing the risk of atrial fibrillation'. Secondary analysis S8: greater on-treatment EPA increase associated with higher AF risk (adjusted HR 1.36 [1.07-1.72]). Class signal: meta-analysis S15 AF HR 1.25 (1.07-1.46), greater at >1 g/day. An AF excess does not plausibly explain a neutral MACE result over 2 years.

safety_signals.quote: Major bleeding occurred in 54 (10.7%) and 56 (11.0%) in the n-3 PUFA and placebo groups, respectively (P=0.87).
safety_signals.note: Despite 86% on dual antiplatelet therapy. S4: 'No patients withdrew from the trial because of bleeding problems.'

safety_signals.value: Point estimates for stroke and MI above 1, none significant: stroke 17 vs 12 (HR 1.37, 0.65-2.88); non-fatal MI 39 vs 35 (1.14, 0.72-1.80)
safety_signals.note: Not a recognised harm; small numbers. Unscheduled revascularization 14 vs 21 (0.66, 0.34-1.30).

genetics.finding: Rare APOC3 loss-of-function mutations lower triglycerides by 39% and are associated with 40% lower CHD risk, supporting causality of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins.
genetics.effect: OR 0.60 (0.47-0.75) for CHD in carriers; TG 39% lower
genetics.quote: The risk of coronary heart disease among 498 carriers of any rare APOC3 mutation was 40% lower than the risk among 110,472 noncarriers (odds ratio, 0.60; 95% confidence interval, 0.47 to 0.75; P=4×10(-6)).
genetics.note: PRE-readout. Abstract read via Europe PMC. Lifelong TG lowering far larger than the 13% median difference in OMEMI.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: triglyceride-lowering LPL variants and LDL-C-lowering LDLR variants give the same CHD protection per 10 mg/dL lower apoB; triglycerides have no independent effect after adjusting for apoB, so the benefit of TG lowering is proportional to the absolute apoB change.
genetics.effect: OR 0.771 (0.741-0.802) per 10 mg/dL lower apoB via LPL score (about 70 mg/dL TG); TG adjusted for apoB OR 1.014 (0.965-1.065)
genetics.quote: Triglyceride-lowering LPL variants and LDL-C-lowering LDLR variants were associated with similar lower risk of CHD per unit difference in ApoB. Therefore, the clinical benefit of lowering triglyceride and LDL-C levels may be proportional to the absolute change in ApoB.
genetics.note: PRE-readout. Abstract read via Europe PMC. LPL score: 69.9 mg/dL lower TG per 10 mg/dL lower apoB. DERIVED: OMEMI TG -14.7 mg/dL corresponds to about -2.1 mg/dL apoB, i.e. a lifelong-genetic OR of about 0.95; a 2-year trial effect would be smaller still.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization (UK Biobank allele scores and CARDIoGRAMplusC4D): higher genetically predicted EPA levels associated with lower CAD risk.
genetics.effect: EPA: lower CAD risk (direction only; abstract gives no estimate)
genetics.quote: Higher genetically predicted eicosapentaenoic acid and dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid levels were significantly associated with a lower risk of CAD both in the allele-score-based and summary-level MR analyses.
genetics.note: POST-readout. Abstract read via Europe PMC.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization of circulating omega-3 PUFA (UK Biobank GWAS, n=114,999): genetically higher DHA and total omega-3 were not protective; nominal harmful associations attenuated after accounting for LDL-C or excluding the FADS locus.
genetics.effect: no protective effect of genetically higher circulating omega-3 on CVD
genetics.quote: Overall, our Mendelian randomization findings do not support a protective role of circulating PUFA concentration on the risk of CVDs.
genetics.note: POST-readout. Abstract read via Europe PMC. With S13, genetic evidence on omega-3 levels is mixed: target genetics 'uncertain'.

consensus_explanation.summary: Experts read OMEMI as a clean but small neutral trial: 1.8 g/day mixed EPA/DHA for 2 years after MI in 1,014 patients aged 70-82 gave no benefit on the primary composite (HR 1.08, 0.82-1.41) or any component, with good adherence confirmed by serum EPA (+87%). The investigators concluded, together with VITAL, ASCEND and STRENGTH, that mixed n-3 supplements are ineffective for cardiovascular prevention, and that only very high-dose ethyl-EPA (REDUCE-IT) may protect, with dose, DHA and placebo choice unresolved. The quantifiable lipid effect was tiny: a 13% median triglyceride difference from a normal baseline of 1.26 mmol/L and no LDL-C change, which under the apoB model predicts almost no benefit, while the trial was sized for a 25% reduction. The authors also said they could not rule out a type 2 error, because recruitment stopped at 1,027 of 1,100 planned and the event rate was about 20% instead of the assumed 35% after heart-failure hospitalization was added mid-trial. An outside expert (Virani) said the population was wrong for a triglyceride drug, as patients were not selected for high triglycerides (mean 111 mg/dL) and were already on intensive modern secondary prevention, so the incremental benefit would be low; high background omega-3 levels in Norway (41% already took supplements) added to this. A numerical excess of atrial fibrillation (HR 1.84, P=0.06) was seen as a possible harm but not as the reason for the neutral result.
consensus_explanation.review_note: Primary effect_too_small: the only sized mechanism (TG-rich lipoprotein / apoB lowering) is causal by genetics but was moved trivially at 1.8 g/day in normotriglyceridemic patients, and the trial had low power for any realistic effect. population is secondary (no TG enrichment, high background omega-3 intake, older patients on modern therapy: Virani, S7; S4 Discussion). design_or_endpoint is secondary (underpowered after a mid-trial endpoint amendment and shortfall in events and recruitment; endpoint includes all-cause death and HF hospitalisation). biomarker_not_causal was not chosen: the secondary analysis S8 links larger EPA rises to lower MACE, and MR on omega-3 levels is mixed.

pre_readout.note: Facts with a public source dated before readout_date (2020-11-15).
available_before_readout: Registry record: 1.8 g EPA+DHA vs corn oil, age 70-82 after AMI, primary composite including HF admission, enrolment 1027 actual, primary completion 2020-06-26 (S3, first posted 2013-04-29; last update 2020-08-19)
Design paper: 30% assumed MACE reduction, alpha 0.05, 80% power, 611 per group, 1400 total, 2-year follow-up, no interim analyses (S5, 2014-06-13)
APOC3 loss-of-function genetics: TG-rich lipoproteins causal (S14, 2014-06-18)
Ference 2019 LPL/LDLR MR: benefit proportional to apoB change (S11, 2019-01-29)
AHA science advisory: TG-lowering doses of n-3 are >3 g/day; 4 g/day reduces TG by >=30% in very high TG (S10, 2019-08-19)
only_after_readout: Topline: AHA press release, no difference in cardiac events (about 20% in both groups), AF 7.2% vs 4.0% (S2, 2020-11-15 = readout)

Full results: HR 1.08 (0.82-1.41), P=0.60, 108 vs 102 events, EPA +87%, TG -13.2% median difference, LDL-C no change, amended sizing (500 per arm, 25%, 35% event rate), type 2 error caveat (S1 and S4, 2020-11-15)
Expert commentary: Virani on unselected TG and low incremental benefit (S7, 2020-11-15); ACC summary (S6)
Investigator commentary: mixed supplements not recommended; high-dose ethyl-EPA open question (S9, 2021-04-07)
MR on omega-3 levels (S13, 2021-04-28; S12, 2022-06-13); AF meta-analysis (S15, 2021-10-06)
Secondary analysis: larger EPA rises linked to lower MACE and more AF (S8, 2022-01-04)

access_summary.note: Key numbers: n, follow-up, planned events, assumed RRR, power, alpha; baseline TG, LDL-C, HDL-C, SBP; effects TG % and abs, LDL-C %, EPA, DHA; HR, CI low/high, p, events x2. Open full text (author accepted manuscript S4 from the Norwegian national archive NVA, and design paper S5 on PMC): n, follow-up, RRR, power, alpha, baselines, TG and LDL-C changes, EPA/DHA, events (16; TG abs is DERIVED from these). Abstract only (free Circulation abstract S1): the version-of-record HR 1.08, CI 0.82-1.41, P=0.60 (4), which differ slightly from the accepted manuscript (1.07, 0.82-1.40, 0.62). Not found: planned events (1). The Circulation version of record is not open access and was not read in full (publisher PDF returned a bot-check page).

open_questions: Version of record vs accepted manuscript: the Circulation abstract gives HR 1.08 (0.82-1.41), P=0.60 and 21.4% vs 20.0%; the accepted manuscript Results text gives HR 1.07 (0.82-1.40), P=0.62 and 21.0% vs 19.8% (its Table 2 shows 21.4/20.0 with 1.07). The calc file uses the version of record. The full version of record was not read (publisher returned a bot-check page).

No planned event count is published; sizing was by patients (1100 after the amendment, 1400 in the design paper). Recruitment stopped at 1027 and the observed placebo 2-year event rate (about 20%) was far below the 35% assumed after adding HF hospitalization.

DERIVED, not from a source: with 210 events, power for HR 0.75 at two-sided 0.05 is about 55%; under the apoB model (S11) a TG difference of -14.7 mg/dL corresponds to about -2.1 mg/dL apoB and an expected relative risk reduction of only a few percent.

The triglyceride effect is a between-group difference in median percent change (13.2 percentage points), not a placebo-adjusted mean; the absolute value -0.166 mmol/L is DERIVED from the baseline mean. apoB, non-HDL-C, HDL-C change and Lp(a) were not reported.
Follow-up: fixed 2-year schedule; median not reported; mean event-free follow-up about 1.7 years DERIVED from event rates per 100 patient-years.

High background omega-3 status (41% used supplements at baseline; cod liver oil allowed in about 20% during the trial; baseline EPA much higher than US values) may have narrowed the contrast; placebo-arm EPA fell 13%, partly because supplement use dropped (S4).
Whether higher-dose or EPA-only formulations would help elderly post-MI patients is not answered by OMEMI; the investigators (S9) call for an ethyl-EPA trial against corn oil.
The AHA newsroom release (S2) is the meeting organiser's announcement on the presentation day; no separate sponsor (Oslo University Hospital) release dated 2020-11-15 was found.
